deity.en: The twin goddesses Tara and Tarini

bhairava.en: Not named in the Adi Peetha tradition

history.en: The Tara Tarini temple stands on the Kumari hill on the bank of the Rushikulya river, near Purushottampur in the Ganjam district of Odisha, not far from Brahmapur. It is one of the four Adi Shakti Peethas of the Kalika Purana tradition, and is not in the Pithanirnaya or the Ashtadasha list.

story.en: According to the Puranas, Sati, the daughter of Daksha, gave up her life in the fire of her father's sacrifice after he insulted her husband Shiva. Grieving, Shiva carried her body across the world until Vishnu's discus divided it, and each place where a part fell became a Shakti Peetha. Tradition holds that Sati's breasts fell here. Here the goddess is worshipped as the twin deities Tara and Tarini.

en: Tara Tarini is one of the four Adi Shakti Peethas.
The Chaitra Jatra is held on the Tuesdays of the month of Chaitra, when special khichdi bhoga is offered and shared with devotees.
A Sankranti Mela is held at every Sankranti, a day considered very auspicious by Tantric practitioners.

timings.en: No official timings are published; check locally before visiting.

bestSeason.en: The Chaitra Jatra (March to April) is the main festival.
